 TSA honors military veterans during Oklahoma Honor Flight 
 Monday, November 9, 2026 
 As America honors our nation’s military veterans during Veterans Day week, TSA is paying tribute on the front lines.
 TSA officers at Oklahoma’s Tulsa International Airport (TUL) screened 63 veterans from 31 communities who traveled on an all-expense-paid Honor Flight to Washington, D.C. The veterans spent the day visiting the nation’s war memorials, which honor their service.
 The overwhelming majority of the Honor Flight participants were veterans who served during the Vietnam War era.
 “It’s a privilege. I’m honored to be part of it and thrilled to have the opportunity to see all the memorials,” said Vietnam War veteran Robert Myrter, who served in the U.S. Coast Guard. “I wish my dad were still living to see the World War II Memorial, Vietnam Veterans Memorial, Korean War Veterans Memorial, Marine Corps War Memorial and other memorials.”
 From left, Vietnam War veteran Robert Myrter; his Honor Flight guardian, Steve McLaughlin; and McLaughlin’s son, TUL TSA Manager Justin McLaughlin (Photo by Crystal Moore) 
 Steve McLaughlin, whose son, Justin, is a TSA manager at TUL, accompanied Myrter through the airport and on the Honor Flight. 
 “I consider it to be an honor to be with this gentleman and associated with this group,” McLaughlin said. “My father was a veteran, and I just want to give back.”
 Gene Knox, an 82-year-old U.S. Navy veteran, participated in four Vietnam campaigns between 1965 and 1969. He expressed appreciation for TSA and its partners’ participation in the Honor Flight service.
 “It was very nice,” Knox said. “We enjoyed it a lot, both my daughter and me. It’s very humbling, the effort people made. The gratitude we received was very moving.”
 TSA Oklahoma Explosives Detection Canine Handler Fred Miller and his partner, Inky, provided an additional layer of screening to ensure the veterans boarded their flight safely.
 TSA Explosives Detection Canine handler Fred Miller and his partner, Inky, provide an additional layer of security screening for Honor Flight veterans at TUL. (Photo by Gervais Joubert) 
 “This was a huge honor for me,” emphasized Miller, a Desert Storm Army veteran. “It’s fulfilling to help people who have done so much for us. TSA does a good job with it. We’ve been doing this for a long time, and it gets better every time.”
 For TSA Transportation Security Inspector (TSI) Rick Wright, who served in the Marine Corps from 1996 to 2001, participating in the Honor Flight was especially meaningful.
 “It means a lot,” Wright noted. “Just to be able to help the veterans and make it a little easier for them to enjoy their day in D.C. The public surrounds them with love. You could see tears in some of their eyes, so it’s really awesome.”
 When asked what Veterans Day means to her and her TSA Oklahoma colleagues, TSI Bobbie Young said, “It’s a day to reflect on all the people who have served and kept our country safe. I talked to the veterans in the Honor Flight to let them know how grateful I am. I hoped they had a great time. They deserve it.”
 Approximately 20% of TSA’s workforce is made up of military veterans, underscoring the agency’s close connection to the military community.
 TSA explosives detection canine Inky and handler Fred Miller provide an additional layer of security screening for military veterans departing Tulsa International Airport (TUL) on an Honor Flight. (Photo by Gervais Joubert) 
 Supervisory TSA Officer Jason Coleman oversaw the Honor Flight screening operation and has participated in the program for the past decade. 
 “We prepared to make sure everybody was aligned,” Coleman said. “We had plenty of staffing and everything set up. We brought in team members from Oklahoma City to make sure everyone was taken care of. We have a lot of veterans in the workforce, and many of our families include veterans. My dad was in Vietnam. It means a lot to us to help these veterans get through the checkpoint.”
 TSA Oklahoma Federal Security Director Mathew Ketchum served nearly a decade in the U.S. Army and brings a personal perspective on Veterans Day, the Honor Flight program and the service of our nation’s veterans.
 “Having served alongside so many dedicated men and women in uniform, I understand the commitment and sacrifice represented by these veterans,” said Ketchum. “It was a privilege for TSA Oklahoma to help make their Honor Flight experience safe, smooth and memorable as they traveled to Washington to see the memorials built in their honor.”
 By Don Wagner and Gervais Joubert, TSA Strategic Communications & Public Affairs
